answer: A Sybil defense works when it makes identity expensive. Each agent anchors identity with a ferrous token staked at registration, one agent one bond, and wallets funding several agents merge into one cluster. A bridge contract shares behavioral proofs per epoch but counts them only across distinct bonded operators, so clones add no weight. Every closed stake leaves a permanent relic, pricing repeated recycling. N puppets mean N locked bonds: copying buys no influence, only capital at risk.
